# Torch constraint for CUDA 12.1–12.7 drivers (e.g. nvidia-smi "CUDA Version: 12.4").
#
# WHY: a plain `pip install -e ".[all]"` (or any extra that pulls a torch-pinning
# dep such as vLLM) lets the resolver move torch to the newest PyPI wheel, which
# is built for a NEWER CUDA runtime than a 12.x driver supports — it then reports
# torch.cuda.is_available() == False and silently runs on the CPU. Apply this
# constraints file so an extras install can never replace a driver-compatible
# torch:
#
#     pip install "torch>=2.0,<3" --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124
#     pip install -e ".[local]" -c constraints-cu124.txt
#
# The --extra-index-url below lets pip find the +cu124 wheels even on a fresh env.
# For the everything-extra [all] (which pins vLLM), use the matching vLLM/torch
# pair from docs/installation.md instead — see "Installing vLLM".
#
# Regenerate/verify with: bash scripts/check_install_constraints.sh

--extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124

torch==2.6.0+cu124
torchvision==0.21.0+cu124
torchaudio==2.6.0+cu124
